fee.rule: 9% new construction: developer fee (defined as developer fee plus consultant fees) limited to the lesser of (a) $4,000,000, (b) $45,000 per unit, or (c) 13% of total development costs excluding the Developer/Consultant Fee category, MHDC fees and all reserves.
fee.basis: Total development cost excluding developer/consultant fee, MHDC fees and reserves
fee.quote: New Construction Developments are limited to the lesser of: a. $4,000,000; or b. $45,000 per unit; or c. 13% of total development costs (excluding Developer/Consultant Fee category, MHDC fees, and all reserves). [May 2025 summary of changes (https://mhdc.com/media/dgtl3asn/summary-of-changes-for-mhdcs-draft-qap.pdf), same three-part limit in 2026 final QAP and in the December 2025 2027 QAP per search excerpts]

maxFeasibleUnits.evidence: No unit cap found. The $4M fee cap and per-development credit approval limit make large 9% deals harder. Found no 2021-2025 9% new-construction award of 101+ units. The 2026-round approvals list shows mostly smaller deals (e.g. Greendale Senior Village, 39 units, new construction). Only search excerpts were available.

sponsorPath.evidence: 2027 QAP (December 2025) excerpt: 'An application submitted by a developer with no prior experience with MHDC would be evaluated based on the entire Development Team.' The QAP evaluates developers and co-developers, so a co-developer/partner path exists. Caveat: up to 25 points are 'based on a Development Team's prior MHDC performance', which a new entrant cannot earn on its own. Real example: Milhaus received MHDC 4% approval (2026 round) for 194 units at Linwood & Troost; the press release calls it Milhaus's first LIHTC development in Kansas City. Read from search excerpts only.

financingPath.evidence: Annual competitive 9% round: 'Federal 9% LIHTC (Estimated): $18,000,000 annually' (2025 NOFA). 2027 QAP: MHDC 'will allocate approximately 85% of the 9% Credit ... on a population proportionate basis', with a St. Louis Region set-aside of 'at least 25%'. The Kansas City region share was not captured. Competition is heavy: 72 of 82 FY2027 applications were 9%.

access.evidence: A new-to-Missouri developer is scored on its whole Development Team, so a co-developer/partner route exists. However, 25 points depend on prior MHDC performance, and roughly 85% of credit is split by region (St. Louis at least 25%). About 72 applications competed for about $18M in federal 9% credit.

urban.evidence: In Kansas City, 100% at-or-below-60% AMI new construction is being financed nearby (194-unit Linwood & Troost, 4%, plus $1.5M from the KC Housing Trust Fund). 9% deals in the metro tend to be smaller. No rent, vacancy or insurance data was gathered (search budget exhausted).

execution.evidence: The team-experience rule allows a partner route, and an out-of-market developer (Milhaus) completed MHDC approval in Kansas City. No local-presence rule was seen in the excerpts. Kansas City and St. Louis are reachable from Chicago by short flight, St. Louis also by rail or a roughly 5-hour drive (general knowledge; not source-verified).

financingPath.evidence: Missouri's 2026 private activity bond cap is $846,523,035 (Missouri Department of Economic Development, DED), with an allocation calendar running January 1 to November 20. 4% projects go to MHDC first, then are recommended to DED for bonds. The FY2026 4% NOFA ran four rounds through June 3, 2026, and an FY2027 Federal 4% NOFA has been approved. No waitlist or exhaustion evidence was found, but demand data was not found either.

4%.nextDeadline: FY2027 Federal 4% NOFA approved (MHDC NOFA page), round dates not captured. Prior FY2026 4% NOFA: four rounds, no applications after June 3, 2026. 4% can also be filed with the main round (FY2027 deadline August 7, 2026).

access.evidence: Same team-based path. 4% credits are non-competitive per MHDC ('as-of-right credits'), and a first-time-in-KC developer (Milhaus) won approval for 194 units in 2026.

urban.evidence: A 194-unit, 60%-AMI new-construction 4% deal at 3200 Troost (two vacant lots) assembled financing: 4% credits, a Planned Industrial Expansion Authority (PIEA) tax abatement, and $1.5M from the KC Housing Trust Fund. A 2025 hearing filing listed $35,000,000 bond / TDC and $2,290,109 federal LIHTC. No rent or vacancy data was gathered.

execution.evidence: Partner route through the Development Team, with an out-of-market precedent. The fee is about 11.2% of TDC under the example, just above DL3's 10% threshold. Guarantee/capital burden was not researched.

localLeadership.evidence: The city supports affordable deals with tools: the KC Housing Trust Fund awarded $1.5M, PIEA granted an abatement, and the Land Clearance for Redevelopment Authority (LCRA) passed a 2025 resolution authorizing MHDC projects. Named individual leaders were not researched.

notes: No official document could be opened. mhdc.com and other sites were blocked for direct fetch in this session, so every value comes from search-result excerpts and ruleVerified is false. New-construction award counts and >100-unit counts could not be extracted. Credits requested vs available were not found. The KC region 9% set-aside percentage was not captured. Venture/market research was cut short when the session web-search limit was reached; no rent, vacancy, cost, insurance or historic-vibrancy data was gathered.
